Deborah "Debbie" Van Kiekebelt (born March 1, 1954,

Debbie Van Kiekebelt

in Kitchener, Ontario)[1] is a Canadian athlete and sports

Personal information

broadcaster. She was a gold medallist in the pentathlon

Kitchener, Ontario

at the 1971 Pan American Games, and was named that

year's Canadian Woman Athlete of the year. Later, she

became Canada's first female sports broadcaster.[2]

Women's athletics

Representing

Canada

Van Kiekebelt attended Clarkson Secondary School in

Pan American Games

Mississauga, Ontario. During her high school days at

1971 Cali
Pentathlon

Clarkson, she not only captured many Peel regional

Pacific Conference Games

titles, but set records in several events.[1]

1973 Toronto
High jump

Van Kiekebelt finished second behind fellow Canadian

Debbie Brill in the high jump event at the British 1971 WAAA Championships.[3][4]

After her Pan-Am gold medal win in Cali, Colombia, in the pentathlon, She competed in the Long Jump and

Pentathlon at the 1972 Olympic games in Munich. Where she failed to advance to final in the long jump, and

place 15th in the Pentathlon. She won a silver medal in the high jump at the 1973 Pacific Conference

Games; she was appointed to the Mississauga Sports Hall of Fame in 1977. She became the first female

Canadian sports broadcaster, appearing on Citytv and NBC, and was host of six television series.[5]

Van Kiekebelt was a director for the See You In Athens Fund which supported Canadian athletes attending

the 2004 Summer Olympics.[5]
